rooms.5110: The four great streets of the city meet here in a wide round plaza paved with black flagstones, each one inlaid with a thin thread of silver. At its middle rises a slender pillar of carved stone, its whole length worked into climbing spiders and coiling script, and a faint violet fire crawls over its tip without ever burning down. Streets leave the plaza north, east, south and west between towering stalagmite houses. Far overhead the cavern roof is lost in darkness, and the silence presses like the weight of the rock itself.
rooms.5194: Forges stand on either side of this stretch of street, and the clang of hammers rings from the doorways east and west. The black flagstones here are scored and pitted where heavy loads of iron have been dragged along. Warm air spills from both smithies, smelling of hot metal and coal smoke, a strange thing in the cold stillness of the cavern. The street runs north to a junction and south to the centre of the city.
rooms.5195: Here the street splits beneath a carved archway of pale stone, its arc lined with the sigils of the noble houses. One way leads east past the gates of the Third House, the other west toward the Second. Behind, to the south, the road returns to the forges and the heart of the city. Glowing fungus has been coaxed into narrow beds along the kerbs, and its cold blue light pools on the paving like spilled water.
rooms.205115: A tall stalagmite rises from the cavern floor here, hollowed and carved into the many-windowed fortress of the Third House. Its doorway opens to the north, framed by two pillars shaped as rearing spiders with their legs locked overhead. Thin lines of violet faerie fire trace the edges of every balcony and window, so the whole spire glows faintly against the dark. The street turns back west to the junction.
rooms.5181: The entrance hall of the Third House is narrow and high, cut straight into the living stalagmite so that its walls curve inward as they climb. A spiral of shallow steps winds up along the wall toward the main chamber above. The floor is polished black stone set with the crest of a spider clutching a crescent moon. Through the doorway to the south the street lies in its violet gloom.
rooms.205104: This broad chamber fills the hollow heart of the stalagmite, its ceiling vaulted into a point far overhead. Tapestries woven of grey spider silk hang between narrow windows, showing hunts and sacrifices in threads of dull silver. Low couches of dark wood and cushions of violet velvet stand in a ring about a cold brazier. A curving stair climbs on up toward the throne room, and another winds down to the entrance.
rooms.205105: The throne room of the Third House sits near the very tip of the stalagmite, a round chamber whose walls taper to a point overhead. The throne itself is carved from a single block of obsidian, its tall back worked into the shape of a spider's spread legs. Faerie fire burns in a ring of silver bowls set into the floor, washing everything in cold purple light. Narrow windows look out over the dark city, and the only way out is the stair winding down.
rooms.5196: The Second House rises to the north, a cluster of three stalagmites joined by slender bridges of carved stone, each spire pierced by dozens of tiny lit windows. Its doorway is a tall slit framed in adamantite, cold and grey. The paving of the street is laid in a pattern of interlocking webs, worn smooth by countless feet. Westward lies the grander seat of the First House, and the junction is back to the east.
rooms.5182: Cool air moves softly through this entrance hall, drawn in from the street to the south and up through the spires above. The walls are carved with a frieze of armed figures standing shoulder to shoulder, their stone faces cruelly fine, their eyes set with chips of red garnet. A broad stair of black stone climbs up into the main chamber of the house. Small niches along the walls hold glowing fungus in silver cups.
rooms.205108: Three galleries open into this tall chamber, one from each of the joined spires, and slender bridges of stone cross the air between them. Beneath them the floor is a single vast mosaic of a spider descending on a thread toward a kneeling figure. Long tables of black wood stand along the walls, set with silver goblets and plates turned face down. A stair climbs higher toward the throne, and another goes down to the entrance hall.
rooms.205109: The Second Throne stands on a dais of three steps, a seat of grey adamantite padded with black silk and crowned with a fan of iron spider legs. Behind it a window of smoky crystal gives a view across the whole cavern, where the lights of the city glimmer like scattered embers. The air is cool and faintly scented with a bitter incense. A stair spirals down to the main chamber of the house.
rooms.5197: The street widens here into a broad forecourt before the greatest house in the city. The First House rises as a forest of carved stalagmites, so thickly worked with balconies, spires and lace-fine stone that it seems grown rather than built. Its great doorway lies to the west, guarded by a pair of tall adamantite doors left standing open. To the east the street runs back past the Second House.
rooms.5179: The entrance hall of the First House is cold and lofty, lined with columns carved to look like pillars wrapped in web. Banners of black silk embroidered with the house's spider sigil hang motionless from the high ceiling. A grand stair of polished obsidian climbs up toward the main chamber. Through the open doors to the east the violet glow of the street seeps in across the floor.
rooms.205111: This is the grandest hall in the city, a vast space hollowed from the heart of the largest stalagmite. Hundreds of tiny lights of faerie fire hang in the air beneath the vault like a field of violet stars. The walls are carved in deep relief with the long history of the house, battle after battle and sacrifice after sacrifice. A narrow stair climbs higher toward the Matron Mother's chamber, and the grand stair descends to the entrance.
rooms.205112: A short landing of black marble ends before a tall door of dark wood bound in silver, set in the wall to the north. Its panels are carved with a great spider whose legs reach out to the edges of the frame, and its eyes are two cut amethysts that seem to follow anyone who approaches. Twin braziers burn with a low purple flame on either side. The stair winds back down to the main chamber.
rooms.205113: The throne room of the First Matron Mother is a long hall of black stone ribbed with silver, rising to a pointed vault far overhead. The throne of obsidian and bone stands on a high dais, flanked by bowls of violet flame and draped in webs of pale silk. A narrow door in the east wall opens onto a walkway high above the city. The way back lies through the door to the south.
rooms.5192: This slender walkway of carved stone arches out from the First House across empty air, no wider than two people walking abreast. Its balustrade is a lace of interwoven webs cut so finely that the violet light below shines through it. Far beneath, the streets of the city wind between the stalagmite houses like threads of glowing fungus. The walkway runs on east, and a door to the west leads back into the First Throne.
rooms.5193: The ornate walkway bends here as it nears the great temple, and the stone underfoot is worn into a shallow groove by generations of passing feet. Ahead to the east a towering door of gold and adamantite opens onto the temple entrance. The drop on either side is dizzying, and a faint cold draught rises from the city far below. The walkway stretches back west toward the First House.
rooms.5141: The Grand Temple of Lloth opens out in a vast hall of black stone, its ceiling hidden in shadow and hung with thick curtains of web. Pillars carved as the legs of a colossal spider rise in two rows toward the dark, their tips glinting with silver. The golden doors to the south lead out onto the grand stairway, and a plain iron door to the east gives on the slave cells. The hall stretches on north toward the altar.
rooms.5142: Deeper in the temple the webs grow thicker, draped from pillar to pillar in great pale sheets that stir though no breath of air can be felt. The floor is cold black stone, stained dark in long trails that lead north toward the altar. A heavy, coppery smell hangs everywhere, and the silence is so deep that every footstep seems an intrusion. Back to the south the hall opens toward the golden doors.
rooms.5148: The dais rises behind the altar on a broad platform of black stone, its surface splashed and crusted with old blood. Cold silver chains hang from rings set into the floor, and a carved spider of jet crouches at its back, legs spread wide over the whole platform. A narrow door in the west wall leads into the treasury. Back to the south lies the bloodstained altar itself.
rooms.5191: Heat rolls from a great forge set into the back of this low workshop, its coals glowing a deep violet rather than red. Iron racks along the walls stand ready for slim curved blades, hooked spears and coats of fine mail. An anvil of black iron sits before the hearth, its face polished bright by long use. The doorway west opens back onto the city street.
rooms.5190: This forge is older and rougher than its neighbour across the street, its hearth hollowed from the raw rock and blackened by centuries of smoke. A wide stone trough of oily quenching water stands beside the anvil, steaming faintly. Tongs and hammers hang from hooks along the walls, each shaped with a care that makes even tools look like jewellery. The street lies through the doorway to the east.
rooms.5198: The city street runs straight here between rows of slender stalagmite homes, their doorways sealed with screens of carved stone. Faint violet faerie fire outlines the rooftops, and here and there a lamp of glowing fungus hangs from an iron bracket. The paving is smooth and spotless, swept clean by unseen hands. Westward the street opens into the great plaza at the city's centre, and eastward it leads on toward the Fourth House.
rooms.5199: Two buildings face each other across this stretch of street. To the north stands the Fourth House, a squat, heavy stalagmite whose door is barred with bands of black iron, and to the east a tall, narrow tower carved with arcane runes houses the Mages' Academy behind a door of dark crystal. The runes pulse slowly with a soft violet light. The street runs back west toward the centre of the city.
rooms.5180: Bare walls of grey stone and a low ceiling give the entrance of the Fourth House a cramped, guarded feel. Arrow slits are cut into the walls on either side, looking out over the doorway to the south. A tight spiral stair rises up into the main chamber of the house. A single lamp of glowing fungus hangs from a chain, casting a cold blue light over the bare floor.
rooms.205124: The main chamber of the Fourth House is plainer than those of its rivals, a round hall lined with weapon racks and hung with battle standards torn in old wars. A long table of black stone bears a carved map of the cavern, its houses marked with chips of coloured crystal. The stair climbs on up to the throne and winds down again to the entrance. Everything smells faintly of oil and steel.
rooms.205125: The Fourth Throne is a hard seat of grey stone, set on a plain dais and flanked by two tall shields bearing the house's spider and dagger. The chamber is small, its walls bare but for a long crack in the rock that has been carefully filled with silver. A narrow window gives on the dark city, the great temple's spires just visible far off. The stair spirals back down to the main chamber.
rooms.5188: This small home is hollowed from the base of a stalagmite, its single round room no more than a few paces across. A sleeping mat of woven fungus fibre lies against the curving wall, beside a low stone table and a shelf of plain clay bowls. The ceiling narrows to a point where the stone has been left rough. The doorway to the north opens onto the city street.
rooms.205120: The Assassins' Academy is a long, dim hall with no windows, its walls hung with black drapes that swallow every sound. Practice dummies of stitched leather stand in a row, slashed and pierced a hundred times over, and a narrow beam runs the length of the floor at knee height for training balance. The lamps of fungus are shuttered almost closed. The only door opens south onto the city street before the temple.
rooms.5186: The hollowed stalagmite makes a snug, low-ceilinged home, its walls painted with faded scenes of the cavern's bridges and spires. A cold hearth stands in a niche, its stone blackened by years of small fires. A curtain of grey cloth hangs across a sleeping alcove, and a rack of drying fungus fills one corner with an earthy smell. The doorway west leads out to the city street.
rooms.205150: The city street bends sharply here around the foot of a great stalagmite whose base has been left uncarved. To the west a low door of woven iron opens onto the Fungus Forest, and its damp, earthy smell drifts out to mingle with the stale air. The street runs north deeper into the city and east toward the adamantium gates. Faint violet light glows from carvings set along the kerb.
rooms.205101: The street broadens before the city's great adamantium gates, which stand to the south in a wall of black stone cut sheer from the cavern. Spikes of grey metal crown the gatehouse, and a lantern of faerie fire burns above the arch. The street runs east past a large building and west to a bend by the fungus forest. Everything here is built to be defended, and nothing is built to welcome.
rooms.205100: The adamantium gates loom over this guardroom, two vast leaves of grey metal so heavy that only magic could swing them. Their inner faces are engraved with a warning in the drow tongue that runs from top to bottom in tall, angular script. Murder holes pierce the ceiling, and the stone floor is marked with grooves where the gates have turned. The gates open north into the city, while a passage leads east into the Tunnel of Ornate Arches.
rooms.5178: A long tunnel leads away from the gates beneath a series of graceful arches, each carved from the living rock and worked with spiders, webs and twining vines. Faint faerie fire glows along the keystones, making a path of violet lights. The floor is smooth and swept clean of every pebble. The tunnel turns south here, and back to the west lie the adamantium gates.
rooms.5177: The last of the ornate arches stands here, larger than the rest and carved with a great spider whose spread legs frame the passage. Beyond it the worked stone gives way to the raw rock of a chasm, and a thin bridge reaches out across the dark to the east. The tunnel runs back north under its row of lit arches. A cold wind rises from the depths and moans softly through the carvings.
rooms.5176: A thin bridge of stone springs out over a bottomless chasm, barely wide enough for one to walk upon. There is no rail, only a low lip of carved stone on either side, and the darkness beneath swallows every sound. Behind, to the west, a door leads back into the tunnel of arches. The bridge reaches on east into the gloom.
rooms.5174: Three thin bridges meet here on a narrow pillar of rock that rises from the depths of the chasm. One runs north to a dead end in the dark, one south deeper into the maze of spans, and one back west toward the arches. The pillar's top is flat and barely three paces across. Strands of old web stretch between the bridges, glistening faintly.
rooms.5175: The bridge simply stops here, its end broken off jaggedly above the void. Whatever it once reached has long since fallen into the chasm, and only a stump of carved stone juts from the far wall, out of reach across the dark. Pebbles kicked from the edge fall without a sound. The only way is back south along the span.
rooms.5173: The bridge bends here around a column of rock, its surface slick with moisture that drips from somewhere far overhead. Small patches of glowing fungus cling to the column, giving just enough light to see the edge. The span runs north to the meeting of the bridges and west along the chasm wall. Far below, a faint gleam of water may be a river or only a trick of the eyes.
rooms.5172: Another meeting of bridges lies here, where three spans join on a broad slab of rock wedged across the chasm. The slab tilts slightly, enough to make every step uncertain. Spans lead east, west and south, each vanishing into the dark after a few paces. Someone has scratched a small mark into the stone, an arrow pointing south.
rooms.5170: The bridge narrows here until it is barely a hand's width wider than a boot, and the rock beneath it is cracked. Ahead to the south a soft green glow spills from an opening in the chasm wall where the bridge ends. Back north the span climbs gently toward the slab where the bridges meet. The drop on both sides is utterly black.
rooms.5169: This small chamber is hollowed out of the chasm wall and lit by a thick carpet of glowing fungus that covers its floor and walls in soft green light. The air is warm and damp and smells of mould. A door to the north leads out onto the thin bridge, and a low gap in the west wall opens into a hidden tunnel. Carvings of open eyes have been cut above both openings.

5168.description: This tunnel is low and narrow, hidden behind a door of stone made to look like the rock around it. Its walls are rough and unworked, bearing only the marks of crude tools. The air is still and stale, and the only light is a faint green glow leaking from the chamber to the east. The passage leads on west into the darkness.

5167.description: The secret tunnel turns here, and a heavy slab of stone hangs in a groove at its northern end, a hidden door that can be slid aside. Dust lies thick on the floor, marked only by a narrow worn path. The passage runs back east toward the glowing chamber. Water drips somewhere in the dark, slow and steady.

5165.description: The tunnel bends here where three ways meet in the rough rock. To the north the passage opens into a large cave, a wide tunnel runs off west into the dark, and to the south a slab that looks like the wall itself hides a door. The floor is gritty with fallen stone, and a cold draught comes and goes.

5166.description: The tunnel opens into a large cave, its roof lost in darkness and hung with long stalactites that drip slowly onto the stone. Broken stalagmites stand about the floor like the stumps of a felled forest. A shallow pool lies in one hollow, black and perfectly still. The only way out lies back south to the bend in the tunnel.

5164.description: A wide tunnel runs through the rock here, broad enough for a cart, its floor worn smooth by the passage of many feet over long ages. At this end the floor rises steeply, and a slope of rough steps leads up into the dark. The tunnel runs back east to a bend. The walls are cold and slick with damp.

5163.description: The wide tunnel levels out at the top of a steep rise, and the rough steps lead back down into the darkness. Old torch brackets, long rusted, are set into the walls at intervals, though no light has burned in them for an age. The tunnel runs on south, its floor scattered with gravel. A faint smell of smoke hangs in the air, old and stale.

5162.description: The tunnel turns here around a great boulder that has fallen from the ceiling and been left where it lay. The rock overhead is cracked and sagging. The passage runs north, and to the west it squeezes round the boulder and goes on. Water trickles down one wall in a thin, glittering sheet.

5161.description: Here the wide tunnel is crossed by a narrow seam of pale crystal that glints in the faintest light. Someone once tried to cut it out of the rock, and the scars of their chisels are still plain in the wall. The tunnel runs east and turns south, where it grows broader still. The air is cool and very still.

5160.description: The tunnel widens into a broad gallery of rough rock, its floor uneven and its ceiling scarred by old falls. At one side a crumbling slope of stone leads up toward a narrow ledge high on the wall. The way north leads back into the wide tunnel. A distant rumble sometimes shakes fine dust from overhead.

5159.description: A narrow ledge runs along the face of a sheer cliff here, so slim that one must press against the rock to pass. A crumbling slope leads down to the wider tunnel. The ledge creeps on west along the wall, and the drop beside it falls away into black emptiness. Loose stones shift underfoot with every step.

5158.description: The ledge ends here against a jutting buttress of rock, and a steep crack climbs up into a sloping tunnel overhead. Handholds have been worn into the stone by many climbers before you. The ledge runs back east along the cliff face. A faint breath of cooler air drifts down through the crack.

5157.description: This tunnel slopes so sharply that the floor is almost a stair, and the rock is polished slick where countless hands and feet have scrabbled for purchase. At the bottom the passage drops down onto a narrow ledge. At the top a door of rough timber bound with iron is set into the west wall. The walls press close on every side.

5155.description: The dark tunnel meets a crossing here, and a foul stench drifts from a cave to the north. To the east a door of rough timber closes off a sharply sloping passage, and the tunnel runs on south into the dark. The walls are black with soot from ancient fires. No light reaches here at all.

5156.description: The stench in this low cave is overwhelming, a thick reek of rot, dung and stale smoke. The floor is covered in filthy straw and gnawed scraps, and the rock is smeared with crude marks in mud and ash. It is the sort of place where something lives and does not care how. The only way out is south, back into the dark tunnel.

5154.description: The tunnel runs straight and narrow here through black rock that seems to drink what little light there is. The ceiling is low enough to brush the head of a tall traveller. Faint scratches on the walls might be the marks of claws or of tools. The passage leads north and south.

5153.description: The tunnel turns here, and a trickle of water runs across the floor from a crack in the wall, pooling in a shallow hollow. The rock is softer here and has been worn into odd, smooth shapes. The way leads north and west, the air growing damper toward the west. Small pale crystals glint where the water has dried.

5152.description: The dark tunnel ends against a wall of wet rock, where a crude door of driftwood planks lashed together with rope is set in the stone to the south. Beyond it comes the faint, distant sound of waves and a smell of salt. The tunnel runs back east. Moss grows thick along the foot of the walls.

5151.description: This damp alcove sits just inside the cliff face, its walls running with water and its floor slick with green weed. Salt air blows in from the south, where a gap in the rock opens onto a rocky shore and the grey sea beyond. A plank door to the north leads into a dark tunnel. The roar of the surf echoes strangely in the narrow space.

rooms.5171: This thin bridge runs only a short way from the slab before it ends against the sheer chasm wall. A doorway was carved there once, framed with spiders, but it has been sealed with a slab of stone fused smooth as glass. The way back lies east to where the bridges meet. A soft, cold wind blows up from the depths, carrying a faint smell of water.
rooms.5184: Giant mushrooms rise here like trees, their pale stalks thick as pillars and their wide caps glowing in soft shades of blue and violet. Spores drift slowly in the still air, catching the light like motes of dust. The ground is soft and spongy underfoot, carpeted with smaller fungi that crunch with every step. A low iron door to the east leads back to a bend in the city street.
rooms.5185: This dwelling is hollowed from a stalagmite of reddish stone, unusual among the black spires of the city. Its single room is bare but for a stone bench and a few hooks on the wall, where a cloak or a lantern might hang. A small window, no more than a slit, lets in a sliver of violet light. The doorway east leads back to the city street.
rooms.5189: The inside of this stalagmite has been carved into a neat little home, its walls polished smooth and set with tiny niches for candles. A low bed of carved stone stands against the far wall, covered with a coarse grey blanket. Bundles of dried fungus hang from the ceiling, giving off a musty smell. The doorway to the east opens onto a bend in the city street.
rooms.5187: This home is carved into the tip of a great stalactite that hangs from the cavern roof until its point nearly touches the street. The room is shaped like an upturned cone, wide overhead and narrow at the floor, and its walls weep slowly with water that is caught in a stone basin. A hammock of woven silk is slung across the space. The doorway opens east onto the city street.

5110.description: The pillar is no thicker than a drow's waist yet rises higher than a house. Spiders of every size climb its length among lines of angular script praising the Spider Queen, and the violet flame at its tip flickers as if to mark the passing hours.

205112.description: The carved spider covers the whole door, its legs curling round the silver bands. Its two amethyst eyes catch the brazier light, and from any part of the landing they seem to be looking straight at you.

5148.description: The spider is carved from a single great block of polished jet, its body as large as an ox. Old blood has run into the grooves of its legs and dried there black.

205100.description: The angular drow script reads, roughly: Who enters without leave of the Houses feeds the Spider. Beneath it the metal is scored with old scratches, as if someone once tried to tear at it with bare hands.

5172.description: The arrow is scratched shallow and quick, by a blade point rather than a tool. It points along the south span, and beside it someone has added a tiny drawn eye.
